operations.name: attach
operations.label: Attach a pull request to Session
operations.description: Connect the calling Session to a GitHub pull request it produced, so the Session's Changes show it. Attaching it again changes nothing.

reference.description: The pull request: owner/repo#123, its GitHub URL, or just its number for the Project's own repository.

operations.name: discover
operations.label: Find the pull requests of the Session's branch
operations.description: Look on GitHub for the pull requests, open, merged or closed, opened from the calling Session's current branch, and attach each one found. Safe to repeat: earlier attached pull requests stay. Answers found, no-match, branchless, not-github or unavailable.

operations.name: detach
operations.label: Detach a pull request from Session
operations.description: Remove one pull request from the calling Session's Changes, for one that does not belong to it. The Session's other pull requests stay, and the pull request itself is untouched on GitHub.

reference.description: The pull request: owner/repo#123, its GitHub URL, or just its number for the Project's own repository.

operations.name: list
operations.label: List the Session's pull requests
operations.description: Read the pull requests attached to the calling Session, with their title, stage, branch and totals as GitHub reports them.

operations.name: refresh
operations.label: Read the Session's pull requests again
operations.description: Ask GitHub again for the pull requests attached to the calling Session, now: the retry after signing in again or after a failed read. Returns what list does.

capabilities.reason: Reads pull requests as the signed-in person, through the Account the Issue tracker provides.
